name: NBI-1065845
summary: NBI-1065845 is osavampator (ex TAK-653), Neurocrine's oral, once-daily AMPA receptor positive allosteric modulator, in-licensed from Takeda and developed as an add-on to an oral antidepressant in adults with major depressive disorder and an inadequate response to it. The Phase 2 SAVITRI study met its primary endpoint (MADRS change at Day 28, p=0.0159; Day 56 p=0.0016, NBIX FY2024 10-K 0000914475-25-000037). The Phase 3 programme is three 200-patient placebo-controlled acute studies (NCT06786624, NCT06911112, NCT06963021; MADRS change at Day 56; primary completion 2027-07), a 550-patient randomised-withdrawal maintenance study (NCT07196501, 2028-07) and an 850-patient open-label safety study (NCT06966401, 2029-05), with topline data guided for 2027 (NBIX FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007). Price anchor: Vraylar, the largest branded adjunctive-MDD product, at $9,662 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: Auvelity's measured Medicare capture (0.1417% a year) and launch curve, as the book's brenipatide and seltorexant seeds carry them. Neurocrine pays Takeda a royalty in the mid-to-upper teens in the US and low double digits outside it (10-Q 0000914475-26-000037).

therapy_mode.source: NCT07196501 (book trials table): randomised-withdrawal maintenance study of adjunctive NBI-1065845, primary outcome time from randomisation to relapse; NCT06966401: long-term open-label safety study, 850 participants; SAVITRI and the Phase 3 acute studies dose once daily by mouth (NBIX FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007: 'once-daily oral administration of 1 mg osavampator')
therapy_mode.note: An add-on taken daily with the patient's antidepressant for the episode and its maintenance, the same use as the book's seltorexant and brenipatide seeds, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07196501 is a 550-participant randomised, quadruple-masked study whose primary outcome is 'Time from Randomization to Relapse' (estimated primary completion 2028-07), and NCT06966401 is an 850-participant long-term safety study (primary outcome TEAEs, 2029-05). A relapse-prevention design means continuous daily dosing. FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007 (book filing_sections, mdna): SAVITRI 'showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in depression severity at Day 28 and Day 56 with once-daily oral administration of 1 mg osavampator'. Chronic holds, as for the seltorexant and brenipatide seeds

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Vraylar: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $1,135,973,310 over 117,573 beneficiaries = $9,662 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Osavampator's Phase 3 setting is the adjunctive-MDD slot, and Vraylar is labelled 'adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adult patients' (book labels table, Vraylar SPL v32). The only Vraylar efficacy supplement between 2019 and 2025 is dated 2022-12-16 (book supplements table, NDA204370 s9, openFDA). I take it to be the MDD approval, but the table does not name the indication. If so, Vraylar's 2024 Medicare spend includes MDD use, which Caplyta's (MDD label November 2025, per the seltorexant seed) does not. It is also the book's anchor for brenipatide in the same disease, so the two price alike. Rexulti, the other branded adjunctive-MDD atypical, has no row in the book's CMS table. Cross-checks, Part D 2024 (lookup.py demand): Caplyta $9,940 (the seltorexant anchor, 3% higher), Auvelity $4,686, Spravato $23,121. The case against: Vraylar's Medicare spend is mostly schizophrenia and bipolar use. A beneficiary's spend covers about 198 days of therapy (23,309,776 dosage units over 117,573 beneficiaries), so it understates an annual price. Auvelity, the newest MDD-only brand and also glutamatergic, sells for half as much, and payers can put generic aripiprazole and quetiapine first. Vraylar's own Medicare price is negotiated from 2027 (see gross_to_net_pct). No price for osavampator has been published, since it is not approved
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Vraylar, Part D 2024: $1,135,973,310 / 117,573 beneficiaries = $9,661.86, so 0.009662 mm USD per patient-year is right in unit. The same row anchors the brenipatide seed (lookup.py seed Brenipatide: 0.009662). Book labels table, Vraylar SPL v32 (2026-08-20): 'Adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adult patients'. Book supplements: NDA204370 efficacy supplements dated 2017-11-09, 2019-05-24, 2022-12-16 (s9) and four on 2025-12-18, so s9 is the only one between 2019 and 2025. Search: AbbVie announced FDA approval of VRAYLAR as adjunctive MDD treatment on 19 December 2022 (MarketScreener, Pharmacy Times), which ties s9 to MDD, so the researcher's hedge resolves in its favour. Days of therapy: 23,309,776 dosage units / 117,573 = 198.3 per beneficiary, as stated. Cross-checks recomputed, Part D 2024: Caplyta $9,940, Auvelity $4,686, Spravato $23,121. lookup.py demand Rexulti returns no rows, as stated. Comparator choice is a labelled judgement with its case against (mostly schizophrenia and bipolar spend, part-year per beneficiary, cheaper Auvelity and generic atypicals)

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices); the Vraylar anchor is Part D (lookup.py demand Vraylar, part D)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 is the share taken off list, so net is $4,831 per patient-year. Cross-check on this comparator: CMS's negotiated maximum fair price for Vraylar from 2027 is $770 per 30-day supply (book negotiated_prices, cms_mfp, ipay 2027). At 2024 use of 198 days per beneficiary that is $5,089, and the halved figure is 95% of it
gross_to_net_pct.check: Anchor is Part D (lookup.py demand Vraylar, part D), so the house 0.5 applies; direction right: 0.5 off list gives net $4,831 per patient-year. Cross-check recomputed from book negotiated_prices (cms_mfp, VRAYLAR, ipay 2027, effective 2027-01-01): mfp_30des $770. $770 x 198.26 / 30 = $5,088.6, and $4,831 / $5,088.6 = 0.949, so 95% as stated

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: reused from the seltorexant seed (lookup.py seed Seltorexant): NCT03321526, seltorexant vs quetiapine XR as add-on to an SSRI/SNRI, 24-week double-blind phase, all-cause study-drug discontinuation 41.2% on seltorexant vs 47.1% on quetiapine XR (Pinter et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 2026;29(4), doi:10.1093/ijnp/pyag009, PMID 41795948); 1 - (1 - 0.412)^(365.25/168) = 0.6848
discontinuation_pct.note: Judgement: reused from the closest modelled competitor, an oral once-daily add-on in the same adjunctive-MDD setting, over a 24-week window. Osavampator's own data are shorter. In SAVITRI, 161 of 183 randomised (88%) completed 8 weeks of treatment, all arms pooled (Psych Congress 2025 poster 33, hmpgloballearningnetwork.com/node/371481, read from a search summary, page not opened). Annualised at a constant hazard, 1 - 0.88^(365.25/56) = 0.566, which is the case for lower. It was not used because 8 weeks is extrapolated six-fold and the pool includes the placebo half. Also for lower: in MarketScan, 19% of patients on an adjunctive atypical antipsychotic discontinued, against 42% on monotherapy (Jain et al., Drugs Real World Outcomes 2022;9(3):477-486, doi:10.1007/s40801-022-00316-4, PMID 35771409; abstract gives no time window, so not annualised). The case for higher: trial retention usually beats real-world persistence on antidepressant add-ons
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed 41795948 (Pinter et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 2026;29(4), doi:10.1093/ijnp/pyag009): NCT03321526, 24-week double-blind phase, all-cause study drug discontinuation 41.2% on seltorexant vs 47.1% on quetiapine-XR. Recomputed 1 - (1 - 0.412)^(365.25/168) = 0.684789; matches the seltorexant seed row (lookup.py seed Seltorexant: 0.6848). PubMed 35771409 (Jain et al., Drugs Real World Outcomes 2022;9(3):477-486): 'Only 19% of patients treated with atypical antipsychotic-adjunctive therapy discontinued treatment versus 42% of monotherapy-treated patients', no time window in the abstract, as stated. SAVITRI: search confirms 183 adults randomised 2:1:1 to placebo, 1 mg or 3 mg for eight weeks (Neurocrine Psych Congress 2025 release; hmpgloballearningnetwork.com/node/371481 is the poster #33 page). I did not see the 161 completers figure; it sits only in the note's case for lower (1 - 0.88^(365.25/56) = 0.5656 reproduced), not in the value. Reuse from the closest modelled competitor is a labelled judgement with the case both ways

forecast_start_year.source: ClinicalTrials.gov primary completion dates (context file and book trials table): the three acute studies NCT06786624, NCT06911112 and NCT06963021 all 2027-07 (estimated); maintenance NCT07196501 2028-07; long-term safety NCT06966401 2029-05. Neurocrine guides 'initial topline data expected in 2027' (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007) and 'Phase 3 readouts for osavampator in major depressive disorder' among its 2027 milestones (Q2 2026 results, 8-K 0000914475-26-000035)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. No NDA date has been published (searched). Topline in the second half of 2027, an NDA in the first half of 2028 and a standard review for a new molecular entity put US approval in the first half of 2029, so 2030 is the first full year. The seltorexant seed runs from a December 2026 primary completion to a first full year of 2029; the same steps from July 2027 land in 2030. The case for earlier: an approval early in 2029 gives most of 2029 on the market. The case for later: if FDA wants the maintenance study (2028-07) in the filing, or the safety database waits on NCT06966401, approval slips to 2030 and the first full year to 2031
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT06786624, NCT06911112 and NCT06963021 all Phase 3, 200 participants, primary outcome MADRS change at Day 56, estimated primary completion 2027-07 (started 2025-01-22, 2025-03-31, 2025-05-30); NCT07196501 2028-07; NCT06966401 2029-05. FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007 (book filing_sections): 'We have initiated a comprehensive Phase 3 clinical program for osavampator in MDD (with initial topline data expected in 2027)'. Q2 2026 8-K 0000914475-26-000035 exhibit: 'multiple important clinical milestones in 2027, including Phase 3 readouts for osavampator in major depressive disorder'. Seltorexant seed: 2026-12-30 primary completion to a 2029 first full year (verified file), so the same steps from 2027-07 land in 2030; the brenipatide seed, also adjunctive MDD, is 2030 too. H2 2027 topline, H1 2028 NDA, standard NME review, H1 2029 approval, 2030 first full year is a labelled judgement with the case both ways

exus_multiple.source: reused from the seltorexant seed: Spravato FY2025, $210mm international against $1,485mm US (J&J FY2025 10-K 0000200406-26-000016, in the book's asset_revenue_regions for esketamine, sec_fsds)
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Neurocrine keeps osavampator's rights everywhere except Japan (10-Q 0000914475-26-000037), but has no filed ex-US split of its own: it sells INGREZZA 'exclusively in the U.S.' and licenses Asia to Tanabe for a royalty (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007). Spravato is the book's measured split for a depression brand, and the closest modelled competitor uses it. The case for lower, and it is strong: Neurocrine has no ex-US sales force, and the adjunctive-MDD brands book almost nothing abroad. Vraylar shows $9mm international against $3,612mm US in FY2025 (book asset_revenue_regions, AbbVie annual report table 0001551152-26-000008), because Gedeon Richter sells it outside the US, and Caplyta shows $0 against $700mm. If Neurocrine licenses ex-US rights out, it earns a royalty, not sales. The case for higher: the Takeda agreement sets an ex-US royalty rate, which suggests ex-US sales are planned, and an oral pill is easier to launch abroad than an in-clinic spray
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions FY2025, esketamine (sec_fsds, 10-K 0000200406-26-000016): US $1,485mm, NonUs $210mm; 210 / 1,485 = 0.141414, and the seltorexant seed carries 0.1414. Vraylar FY2025: US $3,612mm, International $9mm (annual report table 0001551152-26-000008); Caplyta (lumateperone) FY2025: US $700mm, NonUs $0. Territory: 10-Q 0000914475-26-000037 (book filing_sections): Neurocrine retains 'exclusive rights to develop and commercialize osavampator for all indications in all territories worldwide except Japan'. FY2025 10-K: 'We sell INGREZZA exclusively in the U.S.' and Tanabe holds valbenazine in Japan and other select Asian markets. Labelled judgement with a strong case against (no ex-US sales force; adjunctive-MDD brands book almost nothing abroad), so confirmed under the rule; it also feeds the royalty weighting in economics_share

economics_share.source: Neurocrine 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0000914475-26-000037), Takeda collaboration note: the January 2025 Restated Takeda Agreement converted osavampator from a 50:50 profit share to a royalty-bearing licence, returned Japan to Takeda, and 'we will incur tiered based royalties payable to Takeda in the mid-to-upper teens in the U.S. and low double-digits outside of the U.S. on a blended basis as a percentage of net sales'; Takeda may receive up to $742.5mm in event-based milestones. Amendment release: 8-K exhibit sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/914475/000091447525000006/nbix2025127-exhibit991.htm. Netted at the lowest stated rate, as the book nets every royalty (Ralinepag and disitamab vedotin seeds): US 15% (mid-teens, read as 15% as the vepdegestrant seed reads it), ex-US 10% (low double digits, as the Ralinepag seed reads it), weighted by the exus_multiple: (0.15 + 0.10 x 0.1414) / 1.1414 = 0.143806 of sales. Margin from NBIX's FY2025 filed lines (book financials, edgar_companyfacts, the block.py method): revenue $2,860.5mm, cost of revenues $52.1mm (0.0182), SG&A $1,156.2mm (0.4042), R&D $1,015.7mm (0.3551), so margin = 0.2225 with other_costs_pct taken as 0
economics_share.note: Judgement, and provisional. This is a royalty Neurocrine PAYS, netted as (margin - royalty) / margin = (0.2225 - 0.143806) / 0.2225 = 0.3537. NBIX has no company-level rows in the book yet, so the margin uses the FY2025 filed cost lines and leaves out other_costs_pct, which has not been derived for NBIX. Recompute with the same formula once the rows land. Every point of other_costs_pct moves the share by about 3 points: at other_costs 0.05 the margin is 0.1725 and the share 0.166. Sensitivity to the rate: 14% US gives 0.3931, and 17% US with 12% ex-US gives 0.2638. Not in this field: up to $742.5mm of milestones to Takeda, and the royalty Neurocrine receives on Takeda's sales in Japan. The share is low because the engine charges Neurocrine's company R&D (35.5% of sales) and SG&A (40.4%) on osavampator revenue, which leaves a thin pre-tax margin for the royalty to come out of
economics_share.check: Royalty terms confirmed in Neurocrine's own filings (book filing_sections, 10-Q 0000914475-26-000037 filed 2026-07-31, and the same wording in 10-Q 0000914475-26-000026 filed 2026-05-05): the January 2025 Restated Takeda Agreement converted osavampator from a 50:50 profit share to 'a royalty-bearing license', returned Japan to Takeda, and 'we will incur tiered based royalties payable to Takeda in the mid-to-upper teens in the U.S. and low double-digits outside of the U.S. on a blended basis as a percentage of net sales'; 'Takeda may be entitled to receive potential future payments of up to $742.5 million upon the achievement of certain event-based milestones'; a $37.5mm milestone was expensed as R&D in Q1 2025. The 8-K of January 2025 (0000914475-25-000006, exhibit nbix2025127-exhibit991.htm) surfaced by search with the same terms. RATE: 15% US and 10% ex-US are the lowest readings of the stated ranges and match the book's readings (vepdegestrant reads mid-teens as 15%; ralinepag, PF-08634404 and pozelimab/cemdisiran read low double digits as 10%), so the rate follows the house convention. One nuance: the filing states these as BLENDED rates, not tier floors, so the usual reason for the bottom tier (early sales sit in it) does not apply; the midpoint reading (17% US, 11% ex-US) gives a royalty of 0.162567 of sales and a share of 0.2694 on this margin. METHOD: a royalty Neurocrine pays, netted as (margin - royalty) / margin, the book's method for every royalty paid (seltorexant, pozelimab/cemdisiran, disitamab vedotin, PF-08634404, VLA15, ralinepag), which fits forecast.py (owner_rnpv = rnpv x share; fcff charges cogs, SG&A, R&D and other costs as shares of revenue). ROYALTY SHARE OF SALES CONFIRMED: 0.143806 = (0.15 + 0.10 x 0.1414) / 1.1414, i.e. (0.15 + 0.10 x exus) / (1 + exus); 0.15 if the ex-US multiple is dropped. Recompute the share as (margin - 0.143806) / margin on the final block. Margin recomputed from book financials, NBIX FY2025 FY, edgar_companyfacts: revenue $2,860.5mm, CostOfRevenue $52.1mm (0.018214), SG&A $1,156.2mm (0.404195), R&D $1,015.7mm (0.355078), margin 0.222514 with other_costs 0; (0.222514 - 0.143806) / 0.222514 = 0.353722 (0.353682 on the rounded 0.2225). Sensitivities reproduced: 14% US 0.3931; 17%/12% 0.2638; other_costs 0.05 gives 0.1664. Cautions for the final margin: (1) the slope is r / m^2, 2.9 points per point of other_costs at this margin and steeper below it; (2) the share reaches zero at other_costs_pct 0.0787 (margin = royalty) and turns negative above it; (3) filed operating income was $619.1mm (0.2164), so $17.4mm of FY2025 operating cost sits outside the three lines; (4) Neurocrine acquired Soleno in May 2026 and its Q2 2026 10-Q now reports cost of revenues 'excluding amortization of acquired intangible assets', so the FY2025 lines understate the cost base the final block will carry. Milestones and the Japan royalty received are outside the field, as the note says

prevalence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv: 21,414,000, NIMH from NSDUH, 8.3% of US adults with a past-year major depressive episode)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. Incidence equals prevalence there, so forecast.py reads the pool as each year's own and no untreated_carryover_pct row is needed (as in the seltorexant seed)
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool 'Depressive Disorder, Major': epidemiology.csv carries prevalence 21,414,000 (NIMH from NSDUH, 8.3% of US adults with a past-year MDE). Null is right

incidence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv: 21,414,000, an annual count)
incidence.check: epidemiology.csv carries incidence 21,414,000, equal to prevalence, noted as an annual count (2026-09-24). Null is right, and the note on carryover matches that row

eligible_pct.source: Three filters, applied to the NSDUH past-year MDE pool. (1) Treated: 61.0% of US adults with a past-year MDE received treatment (NIMH, nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/major-depression, NSDUH 2021), the book's brenipatide and seltorexant value. (2) Moderate or severe: the Phase 3 enrols 'recurrent MDD (moderate or severe) or persistent depressive disorder' (NCT06786624 key inclusion criteria, clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06786624, via search). Of 12-month MDD cases in the NCS-R, 10.4% were mild, 38.6% moderate, 38.0% severe and 12.9% very severe on the QIDS-SR, so 89.5% were moderate or worse (Kessler et al., JAMA 2003;289(23):3095-3105, doi:10.1001/jama.289.23.3095, PMID 12813115). (3) Inadequate response to an antidepressant in the current episode (NCT06786624 inclusion): 47% responded to citalopram in STAR*D level 1 among 2,876 US outpatients, so 53% did not (Trivedi et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28, PMID 16390886), the seltorexant seed's value. 0.61 x 0.895 x 0.53 = 0.289354
eligible_pct.note: Judgement: the filters are taken as independent. The label pool is about 6.20mm US adults (21,414,000 x 0.289354). Cross-check: Neurocrine says 'approximately one-third of over 16 million people in the U.S. who live with MDD do not achieve adequate relief with existing antidepressants' (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007), about 5.3mm. Not applied: the trial's 'recurrent' criterion, because adjunctive-MDD labels are written for MDD without that limit (Vraylar: 'adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adult patients', book labels table). That is the case for lower: a label that kept 'recurrent' would cut the pool further. The case for higher: treated patients skew more severe than all 12-month cases, so filter (2) understates. STAR*D level 1 already required moderate or worse depression (HRSD 14 or more). The trial also admits persistent depressive disorder, which lies outside this pool. 'Treated' includes talk therapy alone, while the label needs an ongoing antidepressant. The seltorexant label (0.19398 of the pool, with an insomnia filter) sits largely inside this one, so the two compete for the same patients
eligible_pct.check: Recomputed 0.61 x 0.895 x 0.53 = 0.2893535. (1) 61.0% treated: the book's brenipatide eligible_pct row (lookup.py pool), confirmed by earlier second readers. (2) PubMed 12813115 (Kessler et al., JAMA 2003;289(23):3095-105, doi:10.1001/jama.289.23.3095): 12-month cases 10.4% mild, 38.6% moderate, 38.0% severe, 12.9% very severe on the QIDS-SR, so 38.6 + 38.0 + 12.9 = 89.5% moderate or worse. (3) PubMed 16390886 (Trivedi et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40): QIDS-SR response 47% among 2,876 analysed STAR*D level-1 outpatients, so 53% did not respond. Label match: search of the ClinicalTrials.gov listing for NCT06786624 gives key inclusion 'primary diagnosis of recurrent MDD (moderate or severe) or persistent depressive disorder' and 'inadequate response to oral antidepressant treatments in the current episode'. Label pool 21,414,000 x 0.289354 = 6.196mm; FY2025 10-K (book filing_sections): 'Approximately one-third of over 16 million people in the U.S. who live with MDD do not achieve adequate relief with existing antidepressants', about 5.3mm, as stated. Independence of the filters and the unapplied 'recurrent' criterion are labelled judgements with the case both ways

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Auvelity, as measured in the book's brenipatide seed and reused by the seltorexant seed (lookup.py seed Brenipatide): 16,448 Part D beneficiaries in 2024 and 9,268 in 2023 (lookup.py demand Auvelity). New patients in 2024 = 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,186, over a Medicare pool of 53.1mm Part D enrollees (KFF 2024) x 17.54% with depressive disorders (CMS Chronic Conditions Warehouse, 2022) = 9,313,740, less 9,268 = 0.1417%
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: a 1.0x multiple on Auvelity, the newest oral MDD brand with a clean CMS series and, like osavampator, a glutamatergic mechanism. It applies the rate Auvelity took of its own label pool (all diagnosed depression) to osavampator's narrower pool: 21,414,000 x 0.289354 x 0.001417 = about 8,780 new patients a year at peak. The case for higher: only 2% of 455,082 newly diagnosed MDD patients in MarketScan received an adjunctive atypical antipsychotic regimen in the study window (Jain et al. 2022, PMID 35771409), which leaves room for an add-on without the metabolic and movement side effects of that class. SAVITRI reported no dissociation or sedation (search summary of the Psych Congress 2025 poster). Neurocrine already sells INGREZZA to psychiatrists. 2024 was also Auvelity's second full year, not its peak. The case for lower: a first-in-class mechanism with only a 183-patient Phase 2 behind it, cheap generic aripiprazole and quetiapine in the slot, and seltorexant and brenipatide competing for the same add-on patients
penetration_peak_pct.check: Recomputed from lookup.py demand Auvelity (Part D 9,268 in 2023, 16,448 in 2024): 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,185.7 new patients; pool 53.1mm x 17.54% = 9,313,740, less 9,268 = 9,304,472; 13,185.7 / 9,304,472 = 0.14171%. Matches the brenipatide and seltorexant seed rows (0.001417); KFF and CCW inputs were confirmed by those seeds' readers. Peak arithmetic: 21,414,000 x 0.289354 x 0.001417 = 8,780 new patients a year, as stated. Jain et al. 2022 (PubMed 35771409): 8,024 of 455,082 (2%) received atypical antipsychotic-adjunctive regimens, confirmed. As on the seltorexant seed, the solve uses the brenipatide stop rate (0.648) for Auvelity's stock; with this asset's 0.6848 it would be about 0.1454%. The 1.0x multiple is a labelled judgement with the case both ways

ramp_steepness.note: Reused measured MDD curve, the only one the book carries. Judgement carried from the seed: one yearly step is read as early exponential growth
ramp_steepness.check: ln(16,448 / 9,268) = ln(1.7747) = 0.5736 (lookup.py demand Auvelity); matches the brenipatide and seltorexant seed rows (0.574)

ramp_midpoint_year.source: reused from the brenipatide and seltorexant seeds: Axsome FY2025 results (8-K, February 2026), Auvelity net sales up 74% in its third full year, Q4 2025 prescriptions up 42% year on year and 8% quarter on quarter
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Reused measured curve. Judgement carried from the seed: half of peak around year 3, resting on one launch
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Matches the brenipatide and seltorexant seed rows (lookup.py seed Brenipatide: 3.0, from the Axsome FY2025 8-K: Auvelity net sales up 74%, Q4 2025 prescriptions up 42% year on year). That 8-K was confirmed by the brenipatide second reader; not re-searched. Reuse is a labelled judgement
